gpu.what: the machine-wide UE render lock (at most ONE rendered UE instance: game clients rendered or -RenderOffscreen, the editor GUI)
gpu.how: Take it with the project script before any rendered UE run and release it right after: source Scripts/lib/ue-render-lock.sh and use its acquire/release (acquire blocks and prints who you are waiting on). The launch scripts (play.sh, playtest.sh, test-*.sh, editor.sh...) take it themselves once the one-ue-client branch is merged. Headless runs (-nullrhi), dedicated servers, commandlets and builds don't need it. Kewky's play.sh preempts agents: if your rendered run is preempted, retry later.

machine_rules: At most ONE rendered UE instance machine-wide (editor GUI, rendered or -RenderOffscreen game client). Take the render lock (Scripts/lib/ue-render-lock.sh, see the GPU rule in the protocol) before any rendered run; if the script is not on main yet, check `ps -eo pid,args | grep -E 'UnrealEditor|Tribulation'` for a rendered instance and wait until it is gone.
One heavy job at a time: before an editor, cook, build or test stack, run `free -g`; wait (and send progress while you wait) if 'available' is under 16 GB or two editors are already running.
Test servers and clients listen on ports below 32768 (the ephemeral range above it collides with outgoing connections).
Never kill, restart or pause processes you did not start (other workers, Kewky's game or editor, the board itself).
